title: Jewish Dream Interpretation from the Bible to Freud
description: Explores the varieties of dream interpretation in the Jewish tradition from the Bible to Freud. Topics to be discussed include dream and transcendence in the religious imagination and neuroscience; dreams and prophecy; the hermeneutics of dream interpretation; lucid dreaming and the syntax of space and time in the dream consciousness.

title: Representations of Jesus in Jewish Thought from Late Antiquity to the Middle Ages
description: Explores the various ways Jesus has been represented in Jewish sources from Late Antiquity through the Middle Ages. Particular interest will be paid to complex interface of the two faiths and the polemical attempts to draw sharp lines distinguishing them. The investigation of the status of alterity will be a key factor in determining the boundaries and the convergence and divergence of the Jewish and Christian portraits of Jesus.

title: Jewish Magic, the Occult, and Western Esotericism
description: Explores the history of magic and the occult in Jewish sources and the influence they have had on shaping the contours of Western esotericism. Topics to be discussed include the nature of language and the shaping of reality, the interface between magic and mysticism, and the role of secrecy in the transmission of and theurgical use of gnosis.

title: Introduction to Jewish Mysticism
description: An introduction to the schools and texts of Jewish mysticism, with particular attention to the Zohar, Lurianic Kabbalah, and Hasidism. Examination of conceptions of god and the Sefirot, Torah, creation, and redemption, along with consideration of the role of meditative techniques.

title: From Superman to Spiegelman: The Jewish Graphic Novel
description: This survey of graphic novels by Jewish authors will include selections of early comics, works by American authors such as Eisner, Spiegelman, and Pekar, and Israeli graphic novels. The seminar-style discussions will address varied themes, including identity, gender, trauma and memory.

title: Jewish Law
description: A survey of the development of Jewish Law from the times of the Bible, through the Dead Sea Scrolls, New Testament, Rabbinic Literature, and medieval literature. The main emphasis in this course will be the development of Jewish Law in Judaism throughout history, raising questions of continuity and change.

title: Gender in Jewish Culture
description: Explores a variety of approaches towards gender in Jewish culture, engaging topics such as the gender of God, gender roles, gender and nationalism, patriarchy, egalitarianism, and gender as metaphor. Readings include selections from the Hebrew Bible, the Talmud, Kabbalah, Yiddish literature, and texts from modern Israeli and Jewish American culture.

title: Identity, Feminism, and Secularism in Hebrew Literature
description: Provides a broad overview of Modern Hebrew literature, spanning from its origins in the eighteenth century to the contemporary era. Aims to shed light on the factors that make this literature distinctive and fascinating. The course delves into various themes, such as Jewish identity, feminism, secularism, and Zionism, while examining the interplay and conflicts between different generations of literary works. The readings for the course comprise a selection of short stories in translation, but will be available in Hebrew for interested students. All lectures and discussions will be held in English.

title: Image of Jews in Film
description: An introduction to the representation of Jews in film. Individual films are contextualized, followed by a discussion.

title: Medicine, Magic, and Miracle: Christianity and Healing in the Medieval Mediterranean
description: Explores religious language, ritual, text, and ceremony in healing practices throughout the medieval Mediterranean. It also looks at the intersections of medical and religious thought about illness and health, particularly from Christian perspectives in the Mediterranean.

title: Readings in Tibetan Buddhist Texts
description: Close readings of the different genres of the classical texts of Tibetan Buddhism in the original Tibetan: philosophy, history, autobiography, religious poetry, ritual, etc. Also provides a hands-on introduction to available digital tools.

title: Gnosticism and Manichaeism
description: Study of Gnostic and Manichaean religions as philosophical and ritual systems, as book religions, and in their interrelations with Christianity, Judaism, Zoroastrianism, and Platonism.

title: Topics in Catholic Studies
description: Various courses on the topic of Catholic Studies, including courses taught by the Tipton Visiting Professor in Catholic Studies.

title: Church, State, and Orthodoxy
description: A survey of the emergence and development of the Roman Catholic Church as an institution with particular attention to the ways in which church leaders defined, maintained, and transmitted a distinctively Catholic understanding of Christian orthodoxy.

title: Global Catholicism
description: An examination of the ways in which Catholic spirituality and religious practice have been shaped by their encounter with various cultures and traditions.

title: Catholicism and Modernity
description: An examination of key concepts in the history of Catholic thought: the sacred/sacraments, tradition, sacrifice, sex, and authority with attention to how these concepts were interpreted and reinterpreted by Catholic thinkers and scholars of religion in the modern era.

title: Catholicism and U.S. History
description: An examination of the emergence and development of Catholicism in the U.S. from a transnational and comparative perspective with particular attention to the impact of the Catholic tradition on the cultural, political, and social life of the U.S.

title: Seminar in Catholic Studies
description: An examination of selected topics in Catholic Studies that bear on larger questions in religious studies, American history, and global studies.
prerequisites_raw: Religious Studies 138 A, B, C or D and permission of instructor.

title: Catholic Tradition
description: An examination of the interplay between experience, authority, and claims of divine revelation through an analysis of case studies in the history of Catholicism from the early church to the Second Vatican Council.
prerequisites_raw: Religious Studies 18 or consent of the instructor.

title: Early Christian Literature in Greek
description: Reading of the New Testament and other first and second century works as illustrations of Greek style, with attention to the development of Koine Greek, influence of the Septuagint, textual apparatuses, and interpretational tools available to the reader of Greek.

title: Coptic Language and Literature
description: An introduction to Sahidic-Coptic grammar, with special reference to the Coptic Gospel of Thomas.

title: Coptic Language and Literature
description: Readings from the Gospel of Thomas and the Sahidic New Testament.

title: Coptic Language and Literature
description: Readings from selected Subakhmimic Coptic texts.

title: Islamic Traditions
description: Introduction to history, doctrines, and practices of the Sunni, Shi'i and Sufi expressions of Islam. Includes study of Qur'an, Hadith literature, religious law, leadership, and holy places.

title: Islamic Religious Texts
description: Reading and analysis of brief Islamic texts selected from the Qur'an, Hadith, and historical texts. Emphasis on key topics addressed in Religious Studies 140A, such as religious belief and practice, law, relations with Judaism and Christianity, Shi'ism, and mystical experience.
prerequisites_raw: Religious Studies 10E or equivalent. Concurrent enrollment in Religious Studies 140A.

title: Religion, Politics and Society in the Persian Gulf Region
description: History of Islam and politics in societies of Saudia Arabia, Iran, and Iraqsince 1500. Emphasis on topics such as Shi'i and Sunni movements, religion and the state, Iranian revolution, economic development, and modernity.

title: Islamic Mysticism and Religious Thought
description: Sufi mystics, ideas, practices, and movements. The relationship of Sufism to other currents of religious thought, such as theology and philosophy in the middle east, Africa, and Asia.

title: Islam in South Asia
description: Examines the religious, cultural, social, and political formation of Islam in India, from the twelth century to the present. Special consideration is given to patterns of Islamization and Hindu-Muslim encounters in pilgrimage, mysticism, and music. Religious aspects of Indian nationalisticmovements and the 1947 partition are also discussed.
